title: The Crooked Veil
premise: When the border wards of Thornfell collapse and the stars vanish from the sky, Zephyrine Iversen discovers the wards were not broken but eaten — devoured by the Hollow Regent, a memory-devouring parasite that has worn the king's crown for a decade while the true king sleeps entombed in his own forgotten past. As the last oath-bound swordspeaker, Zephyrine carries living memories in her blade, making her both the parasite's greatest threat and its most tempting meal. Guided by a disgraced wardwright and a boy who remembers nothing of himself, she must reach the buried king before the thirteenth moon-turn completes and unbind him — at the cost of surrendering her own most cherished memories to reforge the veil between worlds. In the end she frees the king but loses her name, her oaths, and every road she ever knew, choosing an unwritten future over the survival that was costing her everything.
about_author: August Ishikawa is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent six years mapping mountain passes before turning to fiction, a trade that left them obsessed with borders and the things that cross them. They write fantasy about people who carry too much history and not enough home.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Zephyrine Iversen guides a smuggler's caravan through the Thornfell passes when the stars extinguish overhead and the border wards die with a sound like breaking glass. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: unease hardening into dread as her oath-blade begins to whisper in a voice she hasn't heard since childhood.

chapters.title: What the Wards Were For
chapters.summary: In the lowland town of Cinderhollow, Zephyrine finds refugees who cannot remember their own children's faces. She seeks out Merric Vale, a disgraced wardwright imprisoned for warning the crown about 'the hungry thing behind the veil.' POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance born of mutual guilt.

chapters.title: The Boy With No Yesterday
chapters.summary: A nameless boy stows away in Zephyrine's wagon, carrying a shard of fallen wardstone fused to his palm. The shard shows him fragments of other people's memories — including one of Zephyrine swearing her first oath. POV: the boy (later named Ash). Emotional beat: tentative trust; two broken people recognizing each other.

chapters.title: The Hollow Court
chapters.summary: Zephyrine infiltrates the capital and witnesses the king at court: beloved, radiant, and utterly wrong — his laughter repeats like an echo, and courtiers leave his presence missing small memories. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: horror wrapped in wonder; the enemy wears a friendly face.

chapters.title: Blade of Borrowed Voices
chapters.summary: Zephyrine learns the truth of swordspeaking: her blade holds the memories of every oath-sworn ancestor, which is why the Hollow Regent's hunger pulls toward her. Merric explains the wards were woven from royal memory — the Regent ate them from inside. POV: Merric. Emotional beat: the weight of inheritance becoming a target on her back.

chapters.title: Thirteen Turns
chapters.summary: Merric deciphers the old ward-laws: the veil can be reforged only by the true king's unbound hand, and the Regent will be permanent once the thirteenth moon completes its turn — eleven weeks away. POV: Merric. Emotional beat: a ticking clock set down with cold hands.

chapters.title: The Road That Remembers
chapters.summary: The trio flees the capital along smuggler roads that literally remember Zephyrine's footsteps, glowing where she walks — and betraying her to the Regent's hollow-eyed hunters. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: the painful discovery that belonging somewhere means being findable there.

chapters.title: Ash's First Memory
chapters.summary: Ambushed at a river ford, Ash instinctively uses the wardshard to weaponize a dead soldier's remembered battle, saving them all — then collapses, weeping for a grief that isn't his. POV: Ash. Emotional beat: power and violation intertwined; he doesn't know whose sorrow he's carrying.

chapters.title: The Tomb Beneath the Glacier
chapters.summary: Following Merric's research, they reach the glacier vault where the true king's body — or what remains of him — was hidden after the Regent took his throne. The door opens only to an oath-bound blade. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: awe curdling into despair at what waits inside.

chapters.title: The King Who Forgot Himself
chapters.summary: Inside, they find King Aldric alive but hollowed: the Regent consumed his memories years ago and cast the remainder back into his body like an empty coat. He does not know his own name. POV: Aldric. Emotional beat: devastating pity — the man is a ruin asking strangers who he was.

chapters.title: Teaching a King to Grieve
chapters.summary: Zephyrine feeds Aldric memories from her blade — his coronation, his daughter's laugh — rebuilding him piece by piece. Each gift costs her something irreplaceable. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: love as sacrifice; she gives away pieces of herself to make a stranger whole.

chapters.title: The Regent's Offer
chapters.summary: The Hollow Regent speaks through the mouths of hollow-eyed villagers, offering Zephyrine a bargain: her ancestors' memories are a feast it will trade for safe passage and her friends' lives. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: temptation sharpened by exhaustion — survival has always been her religion.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Waystation
chapters.summary: A hunter ambush at a mountain waystation reveals Merric once served the Regent willingly, trading ward-secrets to save his family — who no longer remember him. Ash turns on him; Zephyrine must choose. POV: Ash. Emotional beat: betrayal reframed as desperation; forgiveness as a hard, deliberate act.

chapters.title: The Price of the Pass
chapters.summary: To escape the closing hunt, Zephyrine pays the road itself — the remembering smuggler roads demand a memory as toll — and surrenders her memory of her mentor's face. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: quiet devastation; she is spending herself to keep moving.

chapters.title: What Wears the Crown
chapters.summary: Aldric recovers enough to tell the truth: the Regent is not a demon but the accumulated hunger of every ruler who ever sacrificed memory for power, given form. It cannot be killed — only unbound and refused. POV: Aldric. Emotional beat: responsibility without excuse; a king reclaiming his failures.

chapters.title: The Veil's Crooked Seam
chapters.summary: They locate the original seam in the veil beneath the ruined first citadel, where the wards were first woven. Reforging requires three things: the king's unbound hand, a wardwright's craft, and an oath-blade full of willing memories. POV: Merric. Emotional beat: hope arriving with an invoice attached.

chapters.title: Ash Chooses His Name
chapters.summary: On the eve of battle, the wardshard offers Ash back his stolen identity — he was the Regent's first victim, the king's lost page. He refuses the return, choosing to remain the boy who chose his own name. POV: Ash. Emotional beat: selfhood as decision, not inheritance; the theme of belonging crystallized.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Moon Rises
chapters.summary: The Regent's forces corner them at the citadel as the final moon-turn begins. Zephyrine duels the Regent's hollowed champion — her former mentor, now an empty vessel wearing his skills. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: grief weaponized; fighting someone she loved and already half-forgot.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: At the seam, Aldric places his unbound hand on the veil, Merric rewove the lattice, and Zephyrine pours her blade's ancestral memories into the weave — emptying the sword and herself. The Regent, offered everything it hungered for, gorges and comes apart. POV: alternating trio. Emotional beat: climax as relinquishment, not conquest.

chapters.title: The Empty Blade
chapters.summary: Dawn returns with stars. But Zephyrine remembers almost nothing: not her roads, not her oaths, barely her own name. Aldric, restored, offers her a place at court; she cannot remember why she'd want one. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: hollow victory; survival achieved at the cost of everything survival was for.

chapters.title: Roads Not Remembered
chapters.summary: Zephyrine leaves the capital with Ash, who chooses to stay with her rather than reclaim his old life. Together, two people without pasts walk out of Thornfell on a road neither knows, drawing maps as they go. POV: Ash. Emotional beat: bittersweet tenderness; belonging rebuilt from scratch.

chapters.title: The First New Star
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Zephyrine carves a new mark into a mountain pass — not an oath, just her name, freshly chosen. Her blade hums with one new memory: this moment. Some things, she realizes, are worth surviving for after all. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: quiet resolution; the price paid becomes the foundation of a life honestly owned.
